cards.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, is writing to the twelve tribes scattered abroad (James 1:1). He's just told his brothers to quit playing favorites with the rich and dishonoring the poor (James 2:1-6). Now he asks them what good it is if someone claims to have faith but has no deeds.

cards.question: Someone claims to have faith but has no deeds. James asks a follow-up question about that kind of faith. What does he want to know?
Then James paints a picture of a brother or sister in real need. What are they without?

cards.text: And what if one of you just tells him, 'Go in peace; stay warm and well fed,' but doesn't provide for his physical needs? That's like texting a thumbs-up emoji to a friend whose car just died on the highway, and WOW, he's gonna ride that emoji ALL the way home!

cards.question: James ties his picture back to faith. Faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is ___.

cards.text: Then James says someone will say, 'You have faith and I have deeds.' Like splitting a pair of shoes: you take the left one, I'll take the right one, and we're BOTH hopping to work.

cards.question: James says someone will say, 'You have faith and I have deeds.' How does James answer?

answers.text: He'll show his faith by his deeds

cards.text: Then James says, 'You believe that God is one. Good for you!' Friend, I think that 'Good for you!' comes with a raised eyebrow, and I know a thing or two about eyebrows.

cards.question: Even the demons believe that God is one, James says. True or false: they rejoice about it.

cards.text: James keeps going, and now he gets direct: 'O foolish man, do you want evidence that faith without deeds is worthless?' Ohhh, James is bringing RECEIPTS.
For his first piece of evidence, James goes straight to the top: our father Abraham. He says Abraham was justified by what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar.

cards.question: Abraham offered his son Isaac on the altar. What does James say Abraham's faith was doing alongside his actions?
Abraham's faith and his actions worked together. James says his faith was ___ by what he did.

cards.text: And James says Genesis 15:6 was fulfilled: 'Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness,' and Abraham was called a friend of God. A FRIEND of God! Meanwhile the best name I ever got back in the Millers' junk drawer was 'what even IS this thing?'

cards.question: True or false: After Abraham's example, James says a man is justified by faith alone.

cards.text: Then James says, 'In the same way,' and brings out a second example: Rahab the prostitute. She lived in Jericho, the city Joshua sent two spies to look over (Joshua 2:1).

cards.question: James says Rahab of Jericho was justified by her actions. What did she do?

answers.text: Welcomed the spies and sent them off another way
Turned the spies over to the king
Kept the spies out of her house

cards.question: James wraps it up with one last picture. Faith without deeds is dead, just like what?
